liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **So Sad (To Watch Good Love Go Bad)** (1 review): Reviewer calls this So Sad a nice one-time performance [9]
- **Rosalie McFall** (1 review): Reviewer describes the Rosa Lee here as a good first performance of the song [9]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this Morning Dew among the best they've heard, comparing it to strong versions like 6/14/85 [12]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Reviewer thinks Jerry may be using a wah pedal early in Not Fade Away, sounding tentative, and wonders if it's the first on tape [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **So Sad (To Watch Good Love Go Bad)**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **A Voice From On High**: rare: 5 archived performances [14]
- **Swing Low, Sweet Chariot**: rare: 13 archived performances [14]
- **Truck Drivin' Man**: rare: 14 archived performances [14]
- **Dirty Business**: rare: 12 archived performances [14]
- **Lodi**: rare: 12 archived performances [14]
- **The Only Daddy That'll Walk The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd70-07-11.aud.cotsman.9379.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 34 songs; 193 min; rated 3.27/5 by 15 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience tape below the usual standard on the site, comparable to a multi-generation cassette bootleg, though still worth hearing; Reviewer hears a multi-generation-sounding tape with an audience-recording feel, suited to listening on a boombox outdoors; For the first nine songs, music is only in the left channel; the right carries tape hiss until the acoustic A Voice From On High [2][3][8][9][12]

## Around the show

- The night ran in three parts: an acoustic Dead set, a New Riders set, then an electric Dead set opened by a recorded Night of the Living Dead intro [1]
- Reviewer notes the date's setlist is disputed and says that after checking several sites, the listing here seems correct [4]
- Reviewer, who attended both nights, says this tape is really the 7/12/70 show and that the dates have been mislabeled [5]
- Attendee at a midnight Fillmore East show says Pigpen had laryngitis, so he played but did not sing [6]
- Attendee recalls a deli next door that was open at 7:30 AM [6]
- Attendee says he was there on 7/11 and that the opener was Easy Wind; he believes the 7/11 and 7/12 dates got switched [7]
- High-energy show with acoustic and electric Dead plus the New Riders, giving plenty of Jerry [12]
- Per the attendee, the electric set on 7/11 began with Easy Wind and included a medley of Dancing, Cryptical, Other One and Lovelight [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-07-11.aud.cotsman.9379.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Andrew Clarke and JCotsman; source: Audience [1]
